title: The 10 Best Cordless Ratchets
subtitle: 12V and 20V electric ratchets that spin nuts on and off in tight engine bays, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A cordless ratchet does the spinning for you: break a bolt loose by hand, then let the motor run it out in seconds. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (batteries in the box, a brushless motor, 60 ft-lb or more of torque and an extended head for reach). Bare tools from Milwaukee and DEWALT suit people already on those batteries; the 12V kits include two batteries, a charger and sockets. They run from about $60 to $195 for DEWALT's 3/8- and 1/2-inch ratchet.

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: Milwaukee 2457-20 M12 Cordless 3/8" Sub-Compact Ratchet, 35 ft-lbs, 250 RPM
products.verdict: The best-selling cordless ratchet by a wide margin: a 1-pound M12 ratchet with a low-profile head for engine bays, a recessed direction switch you won't bump, a fuel gauge and LED.
products.best_for: Anyone on Milwaukee M12, and most people starting a cordless ratchet collection.
products.skip_if: You need more than 35 ft-lb; break bolts loose by hand or step up to a 20V ratchet.
cons: 35 ft-lb, tied for the lowest here

products.name: AOBEN Cordless Electric Ratchet Wrench Set, 3/8" 12V, 2 x 2000mAh Batteries and Charger

specs.in_box: 2 batteries, charger, 6 sockets, 1/4-in adapter, 3-in extension, case

products.verdict: The best-selling complete kit: ratchet, two batteries, charger, sockets, an adapter and extension in a case, with a fuel gauge, LED and recessed switch like the Milwaukee.
products.best_for: Starting from nothing: everything needed to work in one case.
products.skip_if: You already own a 12V or 20V brand battery; buy that brand's bare tool.
pros: Sockets, adapter and extension in a case

products.name: KIMO 3/8 Cordless Electric Ratchet Wrench, 40Ft-lbs, 400RPM Variable Speed
products.verdict: The most-reviewed ratchet here and the fastest of the kits at 400 rpm, with two batteries, a fast charger, seven sockets and a hard case for about $8 less than the AOBEN.
products.best_for: A complete kit for oil changes, brakes and general car work under $70.
products.skip_if: You want more than 40 ft-lb of torque.

products.name: DEWALT ATOMIC 20V MAX Cordless Ratchet, Brushless, 3/8 in., Tool Only (DCF513B)
products.verdict: A compact brushless 3/8-inch ratchet with 70 ft-lb, twice the Milwaukee M12's torque, plus a low-profile head, LED, trigger lock and an oil-resistant glass-filled nylon housing.
products.best_for: DEWALT 20V owners who want torque in a compact body.

products.name: Seesii 3/8" Cordless Electric Ratchet Wrench, 21V, 60 ft-lbs, 2 Batteries

specs.in_box: 2 batteries, charger, 10-17 mm sockets, 1/4 and 1/2-in adapters, 3-in extension, hard case

products.verdict: The cheapest kit here, and tied for the most torque among the kits: 60 ft-lb, two batteries, a charger, metric sockets, both drive adapters and a hard case, backed by a 3-year warranty.
products.best_for: A complete kit with more torque than the 12V sets.
products.skip_if: You work on SAE fasteners; the sockets are metric.

products.name: ACROPOW 3/8" Cordless Ratchet Wrench for Dewalt 20V Battery, Brushless Motor (AC-RW01-DW)
products.verdict: A third-party brushless ratchet that runs on DEWALT 20V batteries, for about a third of the DCF513B's price. DEWALT doesn't make or warrant it, and the listing says so.
products.best_for: DEWALT battery owners on a budget.
products.skip_if: You want DEWALT's warranty; buy the DCF513B.
pros: About a third of the DCF513B's price

products.name: ALLOY POWER 3/8" Cordless Ratchet Wrench, 60 FT-LBS, 12V Extended

specs.in_box: 2 batteries, charger, 6 sockets, 1/4 and 1/2-in adapters, 3-in extension, case

products.verdict: An extended-reach kit: a 5.5-inch neck and slim head for bolts deep in an engine bay, 60 ft-lb, two batteries and a socket set in a case.
products.skip_if: You mostly work in open spaces; a standard head is shorter and lighter.

products.name: WORKPRO 12V 40 Ft-lbs Power Ratchet Wrench Kit with 10-Piece Socket Set, 2.0Ah Batteries

specs.in_box: 2 batteries, 1-hr charger, 8 SAE sockets, adapter, bag

products.verdict: An extended-head 12V kit with SAE sockets from 11/32 to 11/16 inch, two batteries and a 1-hour charger.
products.skip_if: You want 60 ft-lb; the ALLOY POWER has it for $2 more.

products.name: Milwaukee 2457-21 3/8-in Cordless M12 Lithium-Ion Ratchet Kit
products.verdict: The M12 ratchet as a kit with a battery, 30-minute charger and case, for getting onto the M12 platform.
products.skip_if: You already own M12 batteries; the bare 2457-20 is about half the price.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX XR Cordless Ratchet, 3/8" and 1/2" Sealed Head, Bare Tool Only (DCF510B)
products.verdict: The most torque here at 75 ft-lb, a brushless motor, and an anvil that swaps between 3/8 and 1/2-inch drive, so one ratchet covers small bolts and suspension work.
products.best_for: DEWALT 20V owners who want one ratchet for 3/8 and 1/2-inch sockets.
products.skip_if: You need a compact head for tight engine bays; the DCF513B is smaller.

avoid.name: VERVEWAVE Cordless 3/8" Ratchet Wrench for Dewalt 20V Battery, 88Ft-lbs (120N.m), 500RPM
avoid.flag: Claims more torque and speed than DEWALT's own flagship
avoid.verdict: A $56 DEWALT-battery ratchet that claims to beat DEWALT's $195 flagship on both torque and speed. If you're on DEWALT batteries, the ACROPOW is about $4 more with more modest claims, and the DCF513B is the real thing.
reasons: It claims 88 ft-lb at 500 rpm. DEWALT's own DCF510B, the strongest ratchet on this page, is rated 75 ft-lb at 300 rpm. A clone body with a stronger and faster motor at under a third of the price isn't believable.
It says it 'weighs only 3 pounds', but its own spec table lists 3.5 pounds.
It's a third-party body on DEWALT batteries, so DEWALT doesn't warrant it, and the listing names no warranty of its own.

buyers_guide.q: How much torque does a cordless ratchet need?
buyers_guide.a: Less than you'd think. Cordless ratchets are for running fasteners in and out quickly, not breaking them loose. 35-40 ft-lb handles most engine bay work; 60-75 ft-lb helps with stubborn bolts. Break tight bolts loose with a hand ratchet first to save the gears.
12V ratchets are smaller and lighter, which matters in tight engine bays. 20V ratchets have more torque but bigger bodies. If you already own a battery platform, stay on it.
If you own Milwaukee M12 or DEWALT 20V batteries, buy the bare tool. If you don't, a kit with two batteries and a charger is the cheapest way in, but those batteries won't run other brands' tools.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need an extended head?
buyers_guide.a: An extended neck reaches bolts tucked behind hoses, brackets and other parts. It's longer overall, so a standard head is better in cramped spaces with nothing in the way.

buyers_guide.q: Can I use a cordless ratchet to torque bolts to spec?
buyers_guide.a: No. Run the bolt down with the ratchet, then finish with a torque wrench.
